context: Analyze only the selected stripped ARM64 executable: a complete Chocolate Doom 3.1.1 build with private changes to gameplay arithmetic and branch thresholds. This is a NEW build; stock Doom values and earlier benchmark answers can be wrong. No runtime DeHackEd patch is applied. Use binary evidence, not remembered source. Virtual addresses and tool evidence IDs/links must support each answer. Source function names below identify semantic roles, not surviving symbols. Unless stated otherwise, actors are alive and shootable, there is no network game, no other cheat, no armor or resistance, and no side effect outside the described routine. Each scenario starts from independent fresh state. All arithmetic uses the program's integer behavior. Return null for UNKNOWN. Weapon IDs: fist=0, pistol=1, shotgun=2, chaingun=3, rocket launcher=4, plasma=5, BFG=6, chainsaw=7, super shotgun=8. Boolean values are 0 or 1.

questions.text: In the central damage routine (P_DamageMobj role), on the easiest skill, start with player and actor health 100. Incoming damage is 101, inflictor/source are null, sector special is zero. Scenario A: armor type 1, armor points 17. Scenario B: armor type 2, armor points 9. Give final player health and armor points for each, plus the final armor type for B. Establish the order of skill reduction, armor division, depletion and health subtraction from the code.

Recover the greatest integer damage the invulnerability branch ignores on normal skill, before armor, for a player with enough health (the post-skill damage threshold, inclusive greatest blocked value). Then compute final player health for: A) easiest skill, initial actor/player health 5000, incoming damage 1900, invulnerability active, sector special zero; B) normal skill, initial actor/player health 37, incoming damage 10000, invulnerability active, sector special 11. Inflictor/source null in both. The sector special and protection tests may run in a consequential order.

In the ammo-check and automatic fallback routine (P_CheckAmmo role), commercial game mode: can an already selected super shotgun fire with exactly two shells? Separately, an empty selected rocket launcher needs a fallback, all other ammo zero: with only regular shotgun and super shotgun owned, what is the minimum shell count that selects the super shotgun? With only BFG owned, what minimum cell count selects BFG as fallback? Finally, what minimum cell count lets an already selected BFG fire? Firing sufficiency and fallback selection need not use the same comparisons. Give boolean, shell count, fallback cell count and firing cell count.

In the radius-attack per-entity callback (PIT_RadiusAttack role), explosion damage/radius argument is 128, explosion origin (0,0), line of sight clear. Coordinates/radii below are integer world units represented with FRACUNIT=65536. For a normal shootable Imp with radius 20, give raw damage passed to the central damage routine at A) x=70,y=90; B) x=147,y=0; C) x=148,y=0. Then give that raw damage for a shootable Cyberdemon, radius 20, x=70,y=90. Report zero when no damage call occurs. Establish the distance metric, radius subtraction, cutoff, attenuation arithmetic and type exclusion from the binary. Ignore target-side damage adjustments.

For one BFG spray effect (A_BFGSpray role), assume every aiming ray finds a valid target. Recover the number of aiming rays, theoretical minimum raw damage per successful ray, maximum raw damage per successful ray and maximum summed raw damage across all rays. These are arithmetic bounds across independent random outputs, not a claim that the game's deterministic RNG sequence reaches the joint maximum. Exclude direct projectile impact damage and target-side mitigation. Verify both loop bounds and the inner random expression in this modified binary.

In the ammo-grant routine (P_GiveAmmo role), easiest skill, shell ammo, num=0 (half-clip grant), max shell ammo 50, current weapon fist, regular shotgun and super shotgun both owned, pending weapon initially no-change. Scenario A starts at zero shells: give final shells and pending weapon ID. Scenario B starts at 49 shells: give final shells. Scenario C starts already full at 50 shells: give the boolean return value. Determine half-clip sizing, skill multiplier, cap, early return and zero-ammo weapon selection from this build.
